intent.line: Intent: the product owner wants decision seats (Decider voters and objection-window seats) to rotate like card seats, and the runner to enforce it: in the owner's D163 words, "I just want the rotation to even out and don't just jump to all Claude like has happened in the past". D164 chose least-recently-used rotation as the mechanism (a Claude seat refused only while another available model has waited longer, no ratio cap), and each seat starts on a probe under 60 minutes old. Why: audit flag F-070 (audits 56 and 57) found decision seats in decider.py still run with no fresh-probe check, no rotation and no recorded reason, which leaves MD-002 open; this card applies card 208's rules to decision seats so load cannot pile onto Claude unseen.

against: D163 (the product owner's words, quoted verbatim)
D164 C1 (least-recently-used rotation, no ratio cap)
confirmation.note: restates recorded direction and adds no scope

domain_expert.reason: the change applies card 208's rules inside decider.py, covered by the architect and backend developer
the risks are the listed loopholes; the gate runs in the main thread before any worker starts

Criterion 2 is least-recently-used seating over card 208's rotation rules, the check_seat and commit_seat split of gate_seat, pending lines for the voters of one run and an append-only seat-use history, all code and git semantics the architect, QA engineer, backend developer and independent reviewer already hold; criterion 1 showed the card 208 code could be reused through CardRun without a second copy and with no process or Windows problem beyond hygiene already handled (decider.py CRLF kept; scratch cleanup unchanged). The one open choice, whether a Claude voter is judged after the non-Claude voters of the same run, is a reading of D163 and D164 for the reviewer and the Intent confirmation, not outside knowledge. A member can still be added mid-card through a Decider (with its id).

observations: (a) Verified in git: the red a54c9d9's body says, in its existing-tests paragraph, that all other suites listed below stayed green on the prototype, and lists no suites below, only the two tests the green had to change; its failing-run line names tests/test_decider_gate.py alone. What git does show: the structural commit d3826ea measured 140 tests across eleven module groups, not those three suites; the green ed5b0e1 ran the full suite once, 497 OK, which covers what the red did not measure; and the red's prediction 2 was wrong (the clock test needed no change). Cost: none found. The fault is the sentence, not the tests. Not amended (no amends); recorded as a deviation in c0fce24; the criterion 3 adjustment makes every pass or fail claim name its command and count or say 'not measured'.

(b) Not verifiable in git: a turn that ends idle leaves no commit. What git shows around the waits: the facilitator's next commit after a seat result came 30 s after the structural commit (d3826ea 02:44:07Z, the QA line 02:44:37Z), 5 min 44 s after the red (a54c9d9 02:56:04Z, developer line 03:01:48Z; the 03:00 probe was due in between and was taken at 03:00:01Z to 03:00:09Z, 49 min 54 s after the last), and 1 min 50 s after the green (ed5b0e1 03:44:02Z, record c0fce24 03:45:52Z). Commit gaps inside waits were 15 min 36 s, 20 min 31 s and 16 min 6 s with only probe or regeneration commits between, which fits blocking waits and idle turns equally. The measure that matters is the delay from a seat's result to the next facilitator action, and it stayed under 6 minutes each time this cycle. Accepted as reported; the watchdog follow-up belongs to the facilitator.

(c) Verified in the code at ed5b0e1: CardRun.check_seat judges a Claude seat on the history plus the pending lines (facilitator.py line 986), so a same-run codex voter counts as seated, but it returns the history without pending, and commit_seat builds a Claude seat's reason with rotation_reason(self.probes, history) from that history. The reason would say codex was last seated 'never' while the decision counted codex's line from this very run; commit_voters writes codex's line first (judgment order), so the file an auditor reads shows a codex line above the Claude line while the reason says never. The text also contradicts itself (it says Claude was the least recently used and names a model never seated). It has shown in no record because every voter this cycle was Claude (no other model had quota at 02:10, 03:00 and 03:29), so the first exposure would be a live run with a non-Claude voter, which is when an auditor reads it. It is exactly what criterion 3 is about; the developer is right that criterion 3 must account for it.

stand_downs.adjustment: For criterion 3 (the record of rotation: each voter's model, probe time, probe ok flag and evidence, line index and, for a Claude voter, the reason, in decider-result.json and the Decider log entry): a claim comes with the command that produced it, and the record is recomputed from git. (1) Every pass or fail claim in a commit body or the record names the command and the count it came from, or says 'not measured' (the case: a54c9d9 'stayed green'). (2) Red 3 asserts, by value, that for a run with a non-Claude voter and a Claude voter the Claude voter's reason names the other model's same-run line and not 'never' (observation c), and the facilitator commits the confirmation that this reading follows D163 and D164 before the green seat is launched. (3) The green body pastes the output of a recompute command that reads only the Decider log entry and seat-use.jsonl, no probe file, and prints per voter the model, probe taken_at, ok, line index and reason, plus a check that no available model had waited longer than a Claude voter at its line, over the test runs and over the first real run; the number of mismatches is the metric. (4) The D155 tune: the carriage-return check is git diff --cached piped to tr -cd with a CR and wc -c (must print 0); the rev-list count is printed in every in-flight line, seat-written ones included; the facilitator runs the count at each wait line and each seat result and commits a regeneration when it reads 3. Metric: criterion 3 voters whose model, probe time, ok flag, line index or reason cannot be reproduced from the log entry plus seat-use.jsonl alone (criterion 2: 1 known case, the same-run reason; target 0); outcome claims in commit bodies or the record with no command and count, found at review (criterion 2: 1; target 0); in-flight lines without a verified count (criterion 2: 3 of 5; target 0); waits in which the MOB.md count passed 3 without a regeneration (criterion 2: 2; target 0); carriage returns added by commits, counted with tr (criterion 2: 8 lines from the probe writer, 0 typed; target 0 typed, and the probe writer's CRLF rows flagged to the Decider). confirmations.confirmation: Confirmed (stand-down 2 (2), D165): the reading in red 9c8bb71 follows D163 and D164. A Claude voter's recorded rotation reason must name a same-run non-Claude voter's seat-use line (its time and line index) and must not say that model was 'never' seated, because the decision already counted that line when it judged Claude (criterion 2, CardRun.check_seat pending lines). A reason that says 'never' for a model the same run seated misstates the history the rotation was judged on, so an auditor recomputing D163's 'even out' from git would be misled. Not confirmed here, left to the independent reviewer: the top-level probe object in decider-result.json and the 'Probe in force' log line, which go beyond the slice (QA added them because the recompute needs the non-voting models' ok flags); the field names are QA's choice.
